core.title: Store appendices in the appendix subdirectory of the artifact they describe
core.given: An appendix (a mockup, diagram or supplementary file) describes an artifact of the plan structure, wherever it is currently stored.
core.when: You plan, add, move, rename, edit or review it, or come across it.
core.then: Store the appendix in the appendix subdirectory of the artifact it describes, at the level-specific location the profile defines for that artifact's level.
prefer: Use the most specific artifact level the appendix describes, and create that level's appendix subdirectory if it is missing.
Move any misplaced appendix you find to that location, including ones in shared or central folders.
avoid: Placing an appendix directly in the described artifact's own directory instead of its appendix subdirectory.
Storing an appendix at another artifact level or in a shared central folder.
core.why: Co-located appendices keep artifacts self-contained and make supplementary content discoverable relative to the artifact.
evidence: Every appendix file has as its parent directory the appendix subdirectory of the artifact it describes, at the level-specific location the profile defines for that artifact kind. This holds for existing, edited and newly added files, wherever they were found.
verification: For every appendix file, verify that its parent directory is the appendix subdirectory of the artifact it describes, at the level-specific location the profile defines (layout.locations#appendix_dir).

The check is repository-wide: it scans the scope the profile designates for repository-wide checks (roots.scan), not only changed files or the plan tree, so pre-existing misplaced appendices are reported too, including those in shared directories outside the plan tree.
An edit of an appendix already stored in the correct appendix subdirectory is an applicable, passing case, not an out-of-scope one.

Deciding that a file is an appendix, and which artifact it describes, is a semantic step: path-based discovery hints are hints only, not scope gates. Appendix files and the artifact each one describes are identified by the profile's appendix filename pattern (suffix.appendix), whose leading segment carries the artifact identifier. This rule's check then requires that that identifier match the artifact that owns the appendix directory the file sits in; this ownership-consistency requirement is part of this rule's verification, not data of the filename pattern. When the identifier is missing or ambiguous, which artifact the appendix describes is a matter of review judgment (the llm_judged activation fact).

Applicability depends only on which artifact an appendix describes, not on where it currently sits: the change fact identifies violations only, and the rule still applies (and is satisfied) when none is present.

values: appendix file present outside the appendix subdirectory of the artifact it describes
appendix file in the appendix subdirectory of a different artifact level than the one it describes
appendix file stored outside the plan tree (e.g. in a shared or central directory)
an appendix describes a plan-structure artifact that does not match its storage location

fires: A mockup, diagram or supplementary file is added for an artifact of the plan structure.
An appendix file sits directly in the described artifact's directory instead of in its appendix subdirectory, whether it was just added or already existed.
An appendix is stored in the appendix subdirectory of a different artifact level than the one it describes.
An existing appendix describing an artifact of the plan structure is found in an external shared directory outside the plan tree, even if no one moved it in this change.
A reviewer or planner finds an existing misplaced appendix while reviewing or editing, even if it was not touched in this change.
An appendix is moved or renamed.
The content of an appendix that is already stored in the correct appendix subdirectory is edited. The rule applies and is satisfied as long as the file stays there.
doesNotFire: Non-appendix plan artifacts (manifests, workplans, acceptance files) are added or edited in their normal locations.
Unrelated non-appendix code changes are made outside the plan tree, and no appendix describing a plan-structure artifact is added, moved, edited or inspected.

profileRequirements.meaning: For each artifact level, the directory in which appendices describing an artifact of that level are stored: the appendix subdirectory directly under the described artifact's own directory.

The filename pattern by which a file is recognized as an appendix, and how its captured artifact identifier is read: the leading {artifact} segment of the pattern names the artifact the appendix describes, so a check can pair each appendix with an artifact. Pattern data and its reading only; any consistency requirement on that identifier belongs to the rule, not the profile.
profileRequirements.bunValue: {artifact}_{type}_{slug}.ext, e.g. E023_mockup_payment-error.png; the leading {artifact} segment carries the identifier of the artifact the appendix describes (e.g. E023)

neutralityNotes: The concrete directory name 'appendices/' and the four level-specific location templates exist in the core only through the map-key entry layout.locations#appendix_dir (layout.locations is a vocabulary v3 map key; instantiating the entry with the Bun values reproduces bun.json's then, evidence[0] and verifier_detail[1] exactly). The described artifact levels (wagon, WMBT, feature, component) are generalized to 'artifacts of the plan structure' and enumerated by that same entry. Recognizing appendix files and reading the artifact each one describes flow through the vocabulary key suffix.appendix ({artifact}_{type}_{slug}.ext, whose leading segment carries the artifact identifier); per feedback, that key carries pattern data and its reading only — the ownership-consistency obligation (the identifier must match the artifact owning the appendix directory) is retained in core verification and deliberately excluded from the profile value. Only the sibling-rule cross-reference planner.appendix.naming-pattern and the concrete filename example remain bunOnly. The discovery globs of activation.facts[0] and the demo path examples of evidence[1] have no stack-neutral equivalent and remain bunOnly; only their generic principle (hints, not scope gates) survives in verification. bun.json's unless is empty and so is the core's, so no exception was dropped or added; the source declares no automated verifier, and the core's verification describes the check generically without inventing enforcement.
